title: Boolean Logic - AND
concept: The && operator returns true only when BOTH conditions are true.
why: Real decisions often require multiple conditions: 'Is the user logged in AND has permission?' AND lets you combine checks.
syntax_ref: condition1 && condition2  →  true if both are true
tips: `&&` means 'and also' — both conditions must be true
Think of `&&` as a strict gatekeeper that demands both sides pass
Use clear variable names: `is_valid && is_complete` is self-documenting
Short-circuit: if the left side is false, the right side is never evaluated
common_mistakes: Using a single `&` instead of `&&` — single `&` is the bitwise AND operator
Writing `and` instead of `&&` — XIOM uses symbols, not words
Expecting `true && false` to be `true` — AND needs BOTH
